title: 한눈에 ⑥: 누구에게 어떻게 물어요? 의문 어미 정리
objective: Choose the right question ending for the listener and form each one correctly.
summary: An overview of six Korean question endings and which one to use with whom.

task.title: Ask the right way
task.line: Look at who is speaking to whom and what they want, then choose or write the correct question ending.

forms.when: A question inside a longer sentence, before 알다, 모르다, 궁금하다, 물어보다. The speech level comes from the main verb.
forms.means: whether ... / what, where, when ... (an indirect question)
forms.exampleMeaning: Do you know what time the meeting starts?

forms.form: V-나요 / A-(으)ㄴ가요 (ㄹ drops: 살다 → 사나요); casual: V-나?
forms.when: Polite (-요). Use it with strangers, staff, and people you don't know well. Casual -나? is mostly for talking to yourself.
forms.exampleMeaning: Does this bus go to City Hall?

forms.when: Polite with -요, casual without it. Use it to wonder about something, to offer (Shall I ...?), or to suggest (Shall we ...?).
forms.exampleMeaning: Do you think it will rain tomorrow?

forms.when: Casual. Use it only with children, younger people, or very close friends. It sounds kind and a little parent-like.
Mostly casual. Use it when you see what the listener is doing and ask about their plan. Use it with verbs only.
Use it to ask back about what someone just said, because you didn't hear well or you are surprised.
forms.exampleMeaning: You said there's an exam tomorrow?

watchOut: 선생님, 점심 먹었니? (X) → 선생님, 점심 드셨어요? (O): -니 is casual. Never use it with older people or people above you.
얼마나 비싸는지 몰라요 (X) → 얼마나 비싼지 몰라요 (O): use -는지 with verbs only. Adjectives take -(으)ㄴ지.
그 사람이 누구는지 (X) → 그 사람이 누구인지 (O): nouns take -인지 (short form: 누군지).
exercises: Choose the right ending for the listener: ① (to your 7-year-old nephew) 숙제 다 (했니 / 했습니까)? ② (to a stranger on the street) 이 근처에 우체국이 (있나요 / 있니)?
Fill in the blank with -는지, -(으)ㄴ지, or N-인지: ① 이 가방이 얼마나 ____ 모르겠어요. (무겁다) ② 동생이 지금 뭘 ____ 궁금해요. (먹다) ③ 저 사람이 ____ 알아요? (누구)
Complete with -(으)ㄹ까요: ① A: 방이 좀 덥네요. 창문을 ____? (열다) B: 네, 좀 열어 주세요. ② 토요일 오후에는 길이 많이 ____? (막히다)
Your roommate is putting on shoes at 11 p.m. Ask in casual speech, with -게, "You're going out now?": 지금 ____?
Your friend says something surprising. Ask it back with -다고/-냐고/-자고/-라고: ① Friend: 나 다음 달에 회사 그만둬. → You: 회사를 ____? ② Friend: 우리 같이 제주도 가자. → You: 제주도에 같이 ____?
answers: ① 무거운지 ② 먹는지 ③ 누구인지 (누군지)
